Man dies in Bas-Uele after travelling from Haut-Uele, as head of WHO says outbreak on track to be deadliest ever

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to a sixth province, officials have said, a day after the head of the World Health Organization said the outbreak was on track to surpass the deadliest in history, which erupted more than a decade ago and killed more than 11,000 people.

guardian.description:
Hakainde Hichilema is bidding for second term, but feud between him and family of Edgar Lungu, who died in 2025, continues

As Zambians go to the polls on Thursday, the ghost of the current president’s predecessor hangs over the elections.

Hakainde Hichilema, 64, is bidding for a second term leading the southern African country after defeating his arch-rival Edgar Lungu by a landslide in 2021.

guardian.title: At least 44 dead after overcrowded ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe
guardian.description:
Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake

At least 44 people have died after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, police said.

The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales.

South African scientist’s breakthrough research shows soil fungus could be used in fight against devastating crop pest

Hearing about fields full of dead caterpillars enveloped in a mysterious white substance intrigued the South African scientist Letodi Luki Mathulwe. Something was killing off the African armyworm – one of the most devastating pests for farmers in east and southern Africa.

guardian.description:
Flight from Victoria to Toronto forced to return to terminal after repeated attempts to secure child in seat failed

A Canadian airline cancelled a flight from Victoria to Toronto after a child refused to wear a seatbelt.

guardian.description:
Quake of 7.4 magnitude collapses and severely damages buildings in several major cities, including Cali and Pereira

More than 100 people died after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, collapsing and severely damaging scores of buildings in major cities including Cali and Pereira.

guardian.title: ‘Absolutely unacceptable’: Japan condemns visit by Vladimir Putin to disputed Kuril Islands
guardian.description:
Japanese PM says islands seized by Soviets late in second world war are part of her country under international law

The Japanese government has reacted angrily to Vladimir Putin’s first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, which are claimed by both Tokyo and Moscow.

Japan’s foreign minister, Toshimitsu Motegi, summoned the Russian ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev, while the prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, called Putin’s actions “absolutely unacceptable”.

guardian.title: South Korean airport becomes busiest in world for global traffic amid Iran war
guardian.description:
Incheon airport had 38.39m international passengers in first half of 2026, as traffic diverted from Middle East hubs

South Korea’s Incheon airport has become the world’s busiest airport for international passengers, in part owing to disruption in the Middle East caused by the Iran war.

Prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul calls for tighter gun controls and ‘decisive penalties’ after nine dead in school shooting

Thousands of people have been evacuated from areas at risk of flooding and landslides in Beijing, as the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin continue to bring torrential rain to northern and central China.

guardian.description:
The Comac C919 will fly from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, although experts say it could take generations for it to challenge the west’s dominance of the industry

China hopes to break into the world of commercial aviation with the first international flight of a Chinese-made passenger jet scheduled for Wednesday.

The Comac C919 will take off from Beijing capital international airport at 3pm, landing in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, just over two hours later.

euronews.title: One dead, several injured in Rotterdam port blast at Gunvor refinery
euronews.description: The Netherlands is investigating an explosion at the port of Rotterdam that killed one person and injured several others on Thursday, 13 August. The blast happened at about 11:30 a.m. at an oil facility in the Europoort industrial section of Europe’s largest port.

euronews.description: Media reports named the dead man as a Ukrainian navy defector who went on to command a Kalibr missile submarine for Moscow's Black Sea Fleet.

euronews.description: Brussels has transformed its historic Grand Place into a giant floral version of Japan’s Great Wave off Kanagawa, using around 500,000 dahlias laid out over 1,300 square metres of cobblestones.

euronews.title: Poland thwarts unprecedented plot by Russia to kill Ukrainian-US citizen in a NATO country, PM Tusk says
euronews.description: Poland, a NATO and EU member state along the alliance's Eastern flank, has accused Russia of "sabotage" on several occasions since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

euronews.title: These are Europe’s best-value cities for a weekend break - and Poland dominates the top five
euronews.description: A new study has revealed the best-value European cities for a weekend away, with Polish destinations sweeping the top five and some of the continent’s biggest tourist hotspots proving much pricier.

euronews.title: Explosion at Dutch port of Rotterdam leaves one dead and several injured, police say
euronews.description: The explosion happened at a refinery and fuel terminal run by Gunvor Energy in an industrial section of the vast port premises.

euronews.title: Hungary unveils new 'clean up' plan as governemnt takes first steps to unlocking frozen EU funds
euronews.description: Budapest will keep a list of economic operators who are barred from public tenders due to prior economic offences, fulfilling an EU obligation to restoring its access to critical funding.

euronews.title: Byway launches free online course to help you plan out a rail trip across Europe
euronews.description: The course covers things like how to choose the right Interrail pass and how to manage disruptions.

euronews.title: Iran's military rejects Trump's claims of US control over Strait of Hormuz as 'lies'
euronews.description: Iran has kept control of Hormuz, a vital energy conduit, since the outbreak of the war on 28 February, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway.

euronews.title: Trump’s vaccine overhaul could fuel mistrust and leave Europe vulnerable to disease resurgence
euronews.description: The fallout from US President Donald Trump’s executive order aimed at reducing the number of universally recommended childhood immunisations could extend beyond the United States, fuelling vaccine mistrust and creating immunisation gaps.

euronews.title: A tiny hard spot was Lucy Davis’ first sign of breast cancer. What else should you check for?
euronews.description: British actor Lucy Davis almost ignored the first sign of her breast cancer. Here’s what to look out for and when to get screened.

euronews.title: Romania shuts off second reactor at Cernavodă NPP amid low water levels on Danube
euronews.description: Nearly two-thirds of the Danube has seen flow rates that are the lowest on record for a month of July in 34 years, according to an analysis published on Monday by the European climate change observatory, Copernicus.

euronews.title: EU experts on the ground in Ceuta amid fears of fresh migrant influx
euronews.description: A team of EU migration experts is in Ceuta for a “first-hand assessment” of the situation, as reports warn of a potential new migrant influx on 15 August. Brussels, however, says its focus remains on protecting the EU’s external border at all times, rather than on any “specific date”.

euronews.title: Why do women need 12 times their salary to buy a home, when men need only eight?
euronews.description: A consistent pay gap and more difficulties in saving for a deposit compared to men are some of the factors holding women back from home ownership.

euronews.title: Russian forces strike second passenger train in Ukraine's Odesa region
euronews.description: The latest attack comes as the United Nations recorded a record-number of civilian deaths in Ukraine in July, the highest monthly toll since May 2022.

euronews.title: Azerbaijan bets on the pomegranate as its next big export
euronews.description: Azerbaijan is turning pomegranates, a fruit with 2,000 years of cultural history, into a global brand, with €48.2 million in exports and more than 200 cultivated varieties putting it in direct competition with Iran, Turkey and Spain

euronews.title: France accues Iran of 'bloodshed' over use of death penalty
euronews.description: After a statement condemning Iran's use of the death penalty, tensions rose between senior diplomats. Paris accused Tehran of 'bloodshed' and Iran called France's stance 'blatant hypocrisy.'

euronews.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'The End Of Oak Street' - Putting the Jurassic World franchise to shame
euronews.description: A mysterious cosmic event uproots Oak Street from 80s suburbia to prehistoric times... It's the blockbuster surprise of the summer.

rfi.title: France and 30 other countries condemn Iran's executions of protestors
rfi.description: More than 30 countries, including France, the United Kingdom and Canada, have condemned Iran's use of capital punishment, saying in a joint statement on Wednesday the Islamic Republic was executing protesters to "silence dissent". Tehran accused its critics of hypocrisy.

rfi.title: Romania shuts down nuclear plant due to low level of drought-hit Danube
rfi.description: Romania on Thursday began a complete shutdown of its only nuclear plant after levels of water in the River Danube – used to cool the site – fell to a record low, the national nuclear energy company said.

rfi.title: Morocco steps up border security over fears of new mass crossing into Ceuta
rfi.description: Morocco has stepped up security along its borders with the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla after fresh calls appeared on social media urging migrants to attempt another mass crossing, weeks after tens of thousands rushed the frontier.

rfi.title: Sister act ushers underdogs Malawi into WAFCON final against Cameroon
rfi.description: Goals from sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga on Wednesday gave tournament outsiders Malawi a 3-1 victory over Algeria, sending them to the Women's Africa Cup of Nations final – after they qualified for the tournament for the first time this year.

rfi.title: Voters in Zambia to deliver verdict on president's economic record
rfi.description: Zambia are voting in a general election on Thursday which will decide whether President Hakainde Hichilema returns for a second term, after steering the country out of a debt crisis.

rfi.title: Can UK's hard-right Farage bin financial probe with by-election win?
rfi.description: Nigel Farage – leader of the anti-immigration Reform UK party – will be fighting for his parliamentary seat on Thursday, going head to head with parody candidate Count Binface in snap polls. The by-election was called after Farage resigned amid a probe into his finances. But the surprise move threatens to backfire as none of the major political parties has fielded a candidate.

rfi.title: Russia threatens retaliatory seizures of EU ships amid new sanctions push
rfi.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for plans to sell off cargo seized from Russian "shadow fleet" vessels.

rfi.title: French ambassador to CAR disciplined over misconduct allegations
rfi.description: France’s foreign ministry has launched disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to the Central African Republic, following allegations that he repeatedly brought young women to the official residence in Bangui and had sexual relations with some of them.

rfi.title: Millions gather to watch as solar eclipse plunges swathe of Spain into darkness
rfi.description: Millions of spectators – tourists and locals alike – gathered in parks and cities across Spain to see Wednesday's total solar eclipse, the first of its kind in the country in more than a century.

rfi.title: Iran faces growing isolation and uncertain future amid 'dire' economic situation
rfi.description: As economic pressure mounts in Iran, RFI spoke to economist Djamchid Assadi about how this is leaving the country more isolated and strengthening the role of the Revolutionary Guards.

rfi.title: France gripped by latest summer heatwave as drought conditions worsen
rfi.description: Scorching heat continued to spread across most of mainland France on Wednesday, as the Ministry for Ecological Transition met to take stock of the effects of a drought that has been steadily worsening since May.

rfi.title: Hungary elects Orban critic Andras Baka as first president in new political era
rfi.description: Hungarian lawmakers on Tuesday approved former supreme court chief Andras Baka – a prominent critic of Viktor Orban who was ousted during the ex-premier's time in power – as the country's next head of state.

rfi.title: Assisted dying, social media and agriculture put France’s top court in spotlight
rfi.description: France’s Constitutional Council is facing a politically charged end to the summer, with judges due to rule on a series of high-profile laws – including those covering assisted dying, social media use by children, agriculture and public security.

rfi.title: Lebanon becomes first country in Middle East to abolish death penalty
rfi.description: Lebanon’s parliament on Tuesday abolished the death penalty, making it the first country in the Middle East to replace capital punishment with a sentence of life imprisonment with hard labour.

rfi.title: Former Syrian leader Assad sentenced to death in absentia over war crimes
rfi.description: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death after a trial in absentia, convicting him of atrocities committed during the country's civil war. Six of his closest aides were also handed death sentences.

rfi.title: Race to find Ebola vaccine as DR Congo outbreak kills more than 2,000
rfi.description: The latest outbreak of Ebola has killed more than 2,000 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to health authorities. Meanwhile, international efforts have been stepped up to test a vaccine for the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever.

rfi.title: France and EU join international aid effort after Colombia earthquake
rfi.description: France has joined the European Union and a host of countries in offering assistance to Colombia, where volunteers and rescuers are searching for survivors following Monday's deadly earthquake.

rfi.title: May ’68 protest leader Cohn-Bendit pledges support to Glucksmann for 2027
rfi.description: Former Green MEP Daniel Cohn-Bendit, a historic figure on the French left, on Monday gave his support to Raphaël Glucksmann for France’s 2027 presidential election, in an interview with Le Point magazine.

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : Sébastien Lecornu prépare une baisse très limitée du déficit et vise autour de 4,9 % du PIB
lemonde.description: Le premier ministre a prévu de présenter son projet de loi de finances dès le 30 septembre. Selon les informations du « Monde », il s’oriente vers une baisse jugée « réaliste » du déficit, sans réforme majeure ni nouvel impôt. L’objectif de ramener le déficit à moins de 3 % en 2029 semble en passe d’être enterré.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, canicule : un plan d’aide aux agriculteurs touchés par les très fortes chaleurs déployé d’ici à la fin du mois ; 80 départements en vigilance orange
lemonde.description: Ce plan, annoncé par la ministre de la transition écologique, comprendra notamment des aides d’urgence mises en place par les préfets, pour soutenir les trésoreries, aider à l’achat de fourrage et préparer la remise en production. « Ces aides complètent les aides sur les engrais et le carburant déjà déployées », selon Annie Genevard.

lemonde.title: L’agent de la DGSE Yann Vezilier, condamné au Mali à vingt ans de prison, a été gracié
lemonde.description: Après un an de détention, Yann Vezilier, qui était dûment accrédité comme officier de la direction générale de la sécurité extérieure auprès des autorités maliennes, a été gracié jeudi par le chef de la junte, le général Assimi Goïta. Une libération obtenue au terme de plusieurs mois de tractations diplomatiques.

lemonde.title: La prescription sociale, un outil pour améliorer la santé et le bien-être des patients : « J’ai l’impression d’avoir moins de douleurs que quand je me sens seule »
lemonde.description: Mis en œuvre dans une trentaine de pays, ce dispositif visant à lutter contre les effets délétères de la solitude sur la santé en favorisant le lien social, fait l’objet d’expérimentations en France.

lemonde.title: Les pompiers, « très déçus » après avoir rencontré Laurent Nuñez, appellent à une mobilisation d’ampleur fin septembre
lemonde.description: L’intersyndicale des pompiers prévoit « une manifestation statique » les 26, 27 et 28 septembre, place de la République à Paris, qui sera appelée « colonnes de la révolte », selon l’UNSA - Sapeurs-pompiers.

lemonde.title: Le Sénégal et la Gambie redéfinissent leurs frontières communes, héritées de la colonisation
lemonde.description: Le 29 juillet, un accord définitif a été finalisé pour clarifier le tracé des 749 kilomètres de frontière terrestre entre les deux pays, a annoncé le Secrétariat permanent sénégalo-gambien. Cette frontière avait été dessinée « sur une carte à main levée dans un huis clos parisien », le 10 août 1889.

lemonde.title: Ultragauche : derrière l’arrestation de militants suspectés de préparer des actions violentes visant la ligne Lyon-Turin, la coopération entre la France et l’Italie
lemonde.description: Le 27 juillet, huit militants ont été mis en examen à Paris pour « association de malfaiteurs ». Ils sont suspectés d’avoir voulu rejoindre un rassemblement violent, le 25 juillet, dans le Piémont. Des vidéos de surveillance les montrent en train de s’exercer avec ce qui ressemble à des explosifs ou des engins incendiaires.

lemonde.title: VIDEO Éclipse solaire : revivez le phénomène exceptionnel à travers le monde
lemonde.description: Des millions de personnes ont levé les yeux vers le ciel, le 12 août 2026, pour observer l’éclipse solaire partielle ou totale qui a plongé certains pays dans le noir pendant quelques instants, comme l’Espagne ou l’Islande.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Kiev revendique une attaque de drones contre une raffinerie de Gazprom, près de la frontière kazakhe
lemonde.description: « La raffinerie russe Neftekhim Salavat de Gazprom a été touchée », rapporte l’état-major ukrainien, jeudi. Ce complexe pétrochimique est situé dans la République du Bachkortostan, à 1 400 kilomètres de l’Ukraine. Selon les autorités locales, 21 drones composaient cette attaque contre Salavat et 16 d’entre eux ont été abattus.

lemonde.title: Spotify va identifier les artistes « IA » et les exclure de ses recommandations
lemonde.description: La plateforme de streaming audio, à rebours de certains de ses concurrents comme Deezer, reste cependant peu transparente quant à la part de musiques générées par intelligence artificielle qu’elle héberge.

lemonde.title: Les paiements par téléphone sont en forte hausse, mais l’argent liquide résiste
lemonde.description: Deux tiers des entreprises de la zone euro acceptent désormais les paiements par téléphone mobile, deux fois plus qu’en 2024.

lemonde.title: Dans les Vosges, ouverture d’une enquête sur le vol de cloches en bronze dans le village de Robécourt
lemonde.description: Ces cloches d’une ancienne fonderie ont disparu au cours de la nuit du 4 au 5 août, puis ont été retrouvées en très mauvais état. Deux d’entre elles ont perdu leurs anses et ne peuvent plus être mises en mouvement, tandis que deux autres ont été « pulvérisées » à coups de masse.

lemonde.title: En Cisjordanie occupée, Israël inaugure la colonie de Ganim, démantelée en 2005
lemonde.description: Ganim est l’une des quatre colonies israéliennes évacuées par Israël dans le cadre du plan de retrait de l’ancien premier ministre Ariel Sharon en 2005, avec Homesh, Sa-Nur et Kadim, toutes situées dans le nord du territoire palestinien.

lemonde.title: Le gouvernement suisse veut serrer la vis aux banques pour éviter une nouvelle crise, trois ans après la débâcle de Credit Suisse
lemonde.description: Berne veut muscler les pouvoirs du « gendarme » financier. Le renforcement du cadre réglementaire prévoit des amendes, un gel des bonus et une intervention précoce en cas de soupçons.

lemonde.title: Séisme en Colombie : la recherche de survivants entre dans une phase décisive alors que le pays compte déjà 265 morts
lemonde.description: Selon le dernier bilan, communiqué mercredi en fin d’après-midi, le tremblement de terre a fait au moins 265 morts, près de 3 500 blessés et 500 disparus.

lemonde.title: Avec le festival Constellations, Metz, confiée aux mains des artistes, rayonne tout l’été
lemonde.description: Jusqu’au 5 septembre, de jour comme de nuit, l’art s’inscrit à même la peau de la ville, venant ainsi magnifier son patrimoine militaire, religieux et urbanistique.

france24fr.title: Pologne : arrestation d'un ressortissant russe chargé d'"exécuter" un Américano-Ukrainien à Varsovie
france24fr.description: Un ressortissant russe qui aurait reçu "l'ordre" de Moscou d'"exécuter" un citoyen américano-ukrainien à Varsovie a été interpellé, a annoncé jeudi le Premier ministre polonais, Donald Tusk. L'assassinat a été empêché de justesse.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie : des colons israéliens maintiennent le siège de maisons palestiniennes
france24fr.description: Des colons israéliens maintiennent le blocus de plusieurs maisons palestiniennes dans le nord de la Cisjordanie occupée, malgré l'intervention de l'armée israélienne.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Mali : "grâce présidentielle" accordée à Yann Vézilier, un agent de la DGSE condamné à 20 ans de prison
Mali : "grâce présidentielle" accordée à un agent français de la DGSE condamné à 20 ans de prison
france24fr.description: Le chef de la junte malienne Assimi Goïta a gracié Yann Vézilier, un agent français de la DGSE condamné en juin au Mali à 20 ans de prison, selon un communiqué du gouvernement malien publié jeudi sur Facebook.

france24fr.title: Nigéria : le pari des véhicules électriques face à la crise du carburant
france24fr.description: À Lagos, le vrombissement des embouteillages pourrait-il laisser place au silence des véhicules électriques ? Face à la flambée des prix du carburant, certains automobilistes nigérians se tournent vers l’électrique. Mais dans le premier pays producteur de pétrole d’Afrique, la transition reste semée d’embûches.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : deux cheminots tués dans une frappe russe contre un train de passagers
france24fr.description: Un conducteur de train et son assistant ont été tués dans une attaque de drone russe contre un train de passagers dans la région d'Odessa, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, a annoncé jeudi le directeur des chemins de fer nationaux ukrainiens.

france24fr.title: Poutine en visite sur une île revendiquée par le Japon, Tokyo proteste
france24fr.description: Vladimir ​Poutine s'est rendu à Iturup, une île revendiquée par le Japon située à l'extrémité méridionale de l'archipel des Kouriles, près de l'île ​japonaise d'Hokkaido, ont rapporté jeudi les médias russes, une visite qui provoque la colère du gouvernement japonais.

france24fr.title: Reconstruction d'Alep : la capitale économique de la Syrie renaît de ses cendres
france24fr.description: Alep, capitale économique de la Syrie, a été dévastée par les combats qui ont vu s'y opposer les forces rebelles et le régime entre 2012 et 2016. Le séisme de 2023 a également lourdement endommagé la vieille ville. Mais aujourd'hui, la reconstruction est en cours, notamment pour les monuments historiques de la ville.

france24fr.title: Madagascar : des députés du président déchu rallient le pouvoir en place
france24fr.description: 🇲🇬 À Madagascar, une nouvelle formation politique voit le jour. Elle réunit 80 députés issus de l’opposition, dont certains membres de l’IRMAR, le parti de l’ancien président Andry Rajoelina. Cette plateforme se veut un soutien du pouvoir en place.

france24fr.title: Eclipse : à Dakar, passionnés et curieux réunis la tête dans les nuages
france24fr.description: L’éclipse solaire partielle a été observée ce mercredi dans plusieurs pays africains. En Tunisie, le phénomène a atteint 59,06 % d’occultation à Tabarka, tandis qu’à Dakar et dans plusieurs régions du Sénégal, près de 37 % du disque solaire a été masqué. À Dakar, de nombreux curieux se sont rassemblés pour assister à ce spectacle céleste, entre émerveillement et enthousiasme.

france24fr.title: "Territoire oublié de l’État" : après le séisme en Colombie, le Choco face à ses vieilles blessures
france24fr.description: Le puissant séisme qui a frappé lundi l'ouest de la Colombie a fait ressurgir les fragilités du Choco, département pauvre et isolé de la côte Pacifique. Alors que les secours peinent à atteindre certaines communautés, habitants et responsables locaux redoutent qu'une fois l'urgence passée, la région ne retombe dans l'oubli.

france24fr.title: Maghreb : pourquoi la fécondité chute à des niveaux historiques
france24fr.description: Saïd n'a eu que deux enfants afin de leur assurer de bonnes conditions de vie. Kaouthar ne veut pas en avoir du tout pour préserver sa "quiétude". Contraintes économiques, changements sociétaux: Maroc, Algérie et Tunisie connaissent une baisse historique de la fécondité.

france24fr.title: REPLAY - Eclipse solaire sur l'Europe, le nord de l'Espagne plongé dans le noir total
france24fr.description: Point d'orgue de l'éclipse solaire qui étend son ombre mercredi sur une partie de l'Europe, le nord de l'Espagne a été plongé dans le noir en plein jour, lorsque la Lune a entièrement masqué le Soleil, au grand ravissement de millions de personnes émerveillées par ce rare spectacle.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : des colons israéliens assiègent des maisons palestiniennes
france24fr.description: Des colons israéliens ont maintenu mercredi un blocus de maisons palestiniennes dans le nord de la Cisjordanie occupée, malgré la venue d'officiers pour les en déloger, selon un des habitants et un photographe de l'AFP.

france24fr.title: Poutine en visite pour la première fois aux îles Kouriles, disputées avec le Japon
france24fr.description: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine s'est rendu pour la première fois jeudi dans les îles Kouriles, en Extrême-Orient, une visite jugée "absolument inacceptable" par le Japon qui revendique également cet archipel.

france24fr.title: NBA : les Los Angeles Lakers vont être rachetés pour 12,5 milliards de dollars
france24fr.description: Les Los Angeles Lakers vont être rachetés pour la somme record de 12,5 milliards de dollars (10,8 Mds EUR) par Joshua Kushner, entrepreneur et frère du gendre de Donald Trump, et l'ancien patron de Disney Bob Iger, a rapporté mercredi le média américain ESPN.

france24fr.title: Football : le PSG remporte la Supercoupe d'Europe contre Aston Villa (2-1)
france24fr.description: Le PSG, double champion d'Europe en titre, a remporté la Supercoupe d'Europe pour la deuxième année consécutive en battant les Anglais d'Aston Villa 2-1, mercredi soir à Salzbourg.

france24fr.title: La menace des drones militaires en Afrique au cœur d'une conférence à Kigali
france24fr.description: À Kigali, au Rwanda, une conférence consacrée aux systèmes autonomes de défense s’est penchée ce mercredi sur l’essor des drones militaires en Afrique. Devenus un atout tactique majeur, ces appareils posent aussi de nouveaux défis en matière de sécurité et de maîtrise des risques.

nzz.title: Ärzte, Spitäler, Apotheker kassieren 360 Millionen Franken an Medikamentenrabatten ein, die eigentlich den Patienten gehören
nzz.description: Medizinische Versorger handeln mit Pharmafirmen Vergünstigungen aus, liefern sie aber nicht den Krankenkassen ab. Das gilt in der Branche immer noch als Kavaliersdelikt, wie ein Bericht der Finanzkontrolle zeigt.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Karikatur der Woche
nzz.description: Der Karikaturist Peter Gut kommentiert in seinen wöchentlichen Zeichnungen für die NZZ das Weltgeschehen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Ärzte bereichern sich illegal: Jetzt müssen die Krankenkassen in die Verantwortung
nzz.description: Hunderte von Millionen Franken landen in einem intransparenten Rabattsystem jedes Jahr in den Taschen von Medizinern – statt bei den Prämienzahlern. So kann es nicht weiter gehen.

nzz.title: Schwimmer machen gefährlichen Fund in Zürcher Flussbad: Scharfe Handgranate nahe Ufer entdeckt
nzz.description: Am Donnerstagnachmittag haben Spezialisten der Schweizer Armee eine Handgranate aus der Limmat geborgen. Sie stammt aus dem Jugoslawienkrieg.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Wasserknappheit zwingt St. Galler Gemeinde zur Badischliessung +++  1200 Personen aus Camping in Frankreich evakuiert
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

nzz.title: «Das Bild meiner toten Tochter verfolgt mich jede Minute meines Lebens»: Zwei junge Menschen sterben in einer Lawine – nun urteilt das Gericht wegen fahrlässiger Tötung
nzz.description: Im Bergsport ist das Restrisiko immer dabei. Das Regionalgericht in Thun muss entscheiden, ob die Tourenleiter den Unfall hätten verhindern müssen.

nzz.title: Vernichtende Umfrage über die integrative Schule: Die Hälfte der Schweizer Lehrer hält das inklusive Modell für gescheitert, weil es sie überlastet – und die Schüler auch noch schlechter macht
nzz.description: Gerade jene Pädagogen, die am meisten betroffen sind, äussern sich negativ zum Status quo. Der Lehrerverband hält noch am System fest, fordert aber mehr Geld.

nzz.title: Vertrauliche Notkredite: Liquiditätshilfen der SNB für Banken sollen künftig geheim sein – und damit ihr Stigma verlieren
nzz.description: Eine Bank gerät unter Druck und braucht dringend Liquidität von der Nationalbank. Bisher musste sie solche Hilfe sofort publik machen. Geht es nach dem finalen «Too big to fail»-Paket des Bundesrates, soll sie in Zukunft schweigen dürfen.

nzz.title: Erster Besuch auf den Kurilen: Putin verärgert den Nachbarn Japan
nzz.description: Mit seiner Reise auf die umstrittene Inselgruppe demonstriert der russische Präsident geopolitische Entschlossenheit. Dass Putin nach Monaten in Moskau wieder vermehrt die russische Provinz besucht, hat aber auch innenpolitische Gründe.

nzz.title: Albulalinie in Graubünden wegen Erdrutsch gesperrt
nzz.description: Der Zugverkehr mehrerer Linien der Rhätischen Bahn ist bis Freitagabend unterbrochen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - News aus Zürich: Wegen des Borkenkäfers muss die Stadt Uster zahlreiche Bäume fällen +++ Zwölf Schulklassen im Kanton haben noch keine Klassenlehrperson
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: Giorgia Meloni und Mette Frederiksen: Das ungleiche Paar, das Europas Migrationspolitik dominiert
nzz.description: Die rechte italienische Ministerpräsidentin und ihre linke dänische Amtskollegin machen gemeinsame Sache in der europäischen Migrationspolitik – und bringen ihre innenpolitischen Gegner in Verlegenheit.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Drohnen treffen Lager des russischen Versandhändlers Wildberries +++ Stromausfall auf der Krim
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: Trauer um einen geschätzten Kollegen: Langjähriger Sportredaktor Daniel Germann verstorben
nzz.description: Auf seinen Spezialgebieten Eishockey, Tennis und Sportpolitik war Daniel Germann eine journalistische Instanz. Noch mehr bleibt in Erinnerung, wie er Verbindungen zu Menschen schaffen konnte, die von tiefem gegenseitigem Respekt geprägt waren.

nzz.title: Die Schweizer Athletin Audrey Werro stürzt im Halbfinal der Leichtathletik-EM – und steht dennoch im Final
nzz.description: Audrey Werro gilt bei der Leichtathletik-EM als Topfavoritin über 800 Meter. Im Halbfinale stürzt sie und knallt heftig auf die Laufbahn. Die 22-Jährige kann dennoch im Finale antreten.

zeit.title: Lehrermangel: GEW warnt vor Personalkarussell in Sachsens Schulen
Bundesliga: Baur wechselt von Aufsteiger Paderborn zu Celtic Glasgow
Kampfmittelexperten gerufen: Explosionsgefahr wegen Gefahrstoffs in Klinikapotheke
Drohnenabwehr von Bund und Ländern: Innenminister fordern schnelle Ausweitung der Drohnenabwehr
zeit.description: Vor dem Hintergrund der Geschehnisse in Leipzig ist die Innenministerkonferenz zusammengekommen. Die Ressortchefs fordern Tempo beim Ausbau der Drohnenabwehrfähigkeiten.

zeit.title: Polen und die Ukraine: Gefährliche Erinnerungen
zeit.description: Polen und Ukraine sind enge Verbündete. Eigentlich. Aber ihre gemeinsame Geschichte belastet das Verhältnis. Kann die Vergangenheit stärker sein als die Zukunft?

zeit.title: Landtagswahlen in MV: AfD beklagt Schmierereien an Wahlkreisbüro
67. Verhandlungstag: Psychiaterin: Block-Kinder durch Entführung traumatisiert
Urlaubssaison: Polen senkt vorübergehend Mehrwertsteuer für Treibstoffe
Wahlkampf: Feuerwehr-Foto mit AfD-Kandidat Siegmund sorgt für Debatte
Eva Maria Michelmann: »Mein Kopf ist noch immer im Gefängnis«
zeit.description: Eva Maria Michelmann wurde in Syrien von Regierungstruppen festgenommen und für fünf Monate inhaftiert. Jetzt spricht sie über ihre Gefangenschaft und ihre Angst.

zeit.title: Studentische Unternehmensberatung: Die Gen Z ist faul? Sie sind der Gegenbeweis
zeit.description: Alice und Sebastian beraten neben der Uni Unternehmen, auch mal unbezahlt. Warum sie ihre freien Abende dafür opfern.

zeit.title: TV-Duell in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: CDU und Linke kritisieren geplante Debatte zwischen Schwesig und Holm
zeit.description: Manuela Schwesig tritt in einer TV-Debatte gegen den AfD-Politiker Leif-Erik Holm an. CDU und Linke wurden ausgeladen – und vermuten dahinter Schwesigs Einflussnahme.

zeit.title: Filmzensur: Hexenjagd in Hollywood
zeit.description: Das Filmfestival von Locarno erinnert an frühere politische Repressionen, an die Paranoia Joseph McCarthys. Filmemacher dürfen nicht arbeiten. Und die Gegenwart grüßt.

zeit.title: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Toter Buckelwal vor Ostseeküste gefunden
zeit.description: Ein toter, sieben Meter langer Wal wurde am Donnerstagmorgen in der Ostsee vor Rügen entdeckt. Woran er starb, ist bisher ungewiss. Eine Obduktion soll Klarheit bringen.

spiegel.title: Erykah Badu: Erstes Studioalbum seit 16 Jahren mit The Alchemist als Produzenten
spiegel.description: Sie gilt als die »Queen of Neo-Soul«, doch in den vergangenen Jahren war auf Tonträgern nur sporadisch von Erykah Badu zu hören. Dafür half sie bei Geburten. Jetzt kommt neue Musik – und in zwei Wochen sogar ein Album.

spiegel.title: Karoline Leavitt: Angriffslustige Trump-Sprecherin beendet ihre Zeit im Weißen Haus
spiegel.description: Sie war die jüngste Regierungssprecherin in der Geschichte der USA – und vor allem bekannt für ihre angriffslustige Rhetorik gegenüber Journalisten. Die einprägsamsten Szenen im Video.

spiegel.title: Israel: US-Botschafter Mike Huckabee nennt Siedlergewalt im Westjordanland »Terrorakt«
spiegel.description: Tagelang hatten Siedler das Zuhause einer Familie im Westjordanland blockiert. Sonst eher unkritisch eingestellt, findet der US-Botschafter Huckabee jetzt scharfe Worte.

spiegel.title: Dänemark – Ålbæk: Seltener Riesenhai am Kattegat angeschwemmt
spiegel.description: Riesenhaie sind namensbedingt zutiefst missverstandene Tiere. An der dänischen Küste ist jetzt ein totes Exemplar aufgefunden worden. Die zuständige Biologin zeigt sich begeistert.

spiegel.title: Afghanistan: Taliban lassen sechs Menschenrechtler gewaltsam verschwinden
spiegel.description: Seit fünf Jahren regieren die Taliban das Land, immer verschleppen sie Mitarbeitende von Hilfsorganisationen in Afghanistan. Human Rights Watch ist nach einem neuen Fall alarmiert.

spiegel.title: Nicole Kidman wählt auf Ibiza zwischen zwei Optionen für den Abend – Scrabble oder Rave
spiegel.description: Nicole Kidman verbringt den Sommer nach ihrer Scheidung von Keith Urban in Europa. Dort macht sie es sich entweder gemütlich oder bricht um 1 Uhr mit Sonnenbrille und Perücke auf in den Club.

spiegel.title: »James Webb«-Teleskop: Extrem heller Punkt könnte Schwarzes-Loch-Stern sein
spiegel.description: Aufnahmen des »James Webb«-Teleskops zeigen immer wieder rätselhafte rote Punkte. Nun haben Forschende eine bislang unbekannte Art von Objekten entdeckt, die eine mögliche Erklärung liefern könnte.

spiegel.title: Ebola-Ausbruch: Mehr als 2000 Todesfälle in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo
spiegel.description: Alle 30 Minuten stirbt im Kongo ein Mensch an Ebola, nie zuvor hat sich das Virus so schnell ausgebreitet. Es ist den Ärzten weit voraus, die in dem Kriegsgebiet auch noch bedroht werden. Die Uno ruft die Welt zu Hilfe.

spiegel.title: USA: Sitzen bald 2000 Gamer als Fluglotsen im Tower?
spiegel.description: Den USA fehlen Fluglotsen. Um die Lücke zu füllen, hat der US-Verkehrsminister eine Kampagne gestartet, mit der 2000 Gamer für den Beruf gewonnen wurden. Doch es gibt Sicherheitsbedenken.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Dürre in der Landwirtschaft, Ebola in Afrika, Zhu Rongji
spiegel.description: In Deutschland wird das Heu knapp, in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo wütet Ebola, und in Peking wird der Mann betrauert, der Chinas Wirtschaftskraft entfesselt hat. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagabend.

spiegel.title: 65 Jahre Mauerbau in der DDR: Warum Julia Klöckner vor einer »neuen Mauer« warnt
spiegel.description: Die offizielle Gedenkfeier zum Mauerbau in Berlin überschattet ein Thema: die anstehenden Landtagswahlen im Osten und das Umfragehoch der DDR-Nostalgiepartei AfD.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Smilla Kolbe fordert Respekt statt Rassismus online
spiegel.description: »Ich will mir nicht vorstellen, wie das wäre, wenn ich nicht so weiß wäre«: Läuferin Smilla Kolbe geht der Umgang vieler Kommentarschreiber mit ihren Teamkollegen nahe. Im TV forderte sie Respekt für alle ein.

spiegel.title: Dax-Vorstände verdienen im Schnitt 42 Mal so viel wie ihre Beschäftigten
spiegel.description: Ob Adidas, Volkswagen oder Fresenius: Die Riege der Dax-Vorstände hat einer Auswertung zufolge 2025 ein Vielfaches ihrer Mitarbeiter verdient. Noch extremer sind die Managervergütungen in den USA.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Russland tötet so viele ukrainische Zivilisten wie zuletzt im Mai 2022
spiegel.description: So viele zivile Opfer wie im Juli gab es in der Ukraine schon lange nicht mehr: Es waren mehr als 400. Dennoch halten Moskau und Kyjiw humanitären Kontakt und tauschten die sterblichen Überreste getöteter Soldaten aus.

spiegel.title: Italien: Neue Millionenjacht geht vor Sardinien an der Costa Smeralda unter
spiegel.description: Acht Millionen Euro soll die »Angiola II« gekostet haben. Nur Tage nach ihrer Übergabe ist die 30 Meter lange Luxusjacht gesunken. Sie war gerade vor einem Nobel-Urlaubsort unterwegs.

spiegel.title: Thüringen: Sahra Wagenknecht lehnt Björn Höckes Wahlangebot ab und fordert TV-Duell
spiegel.description: AfD-Politiker Björn Höcke will Sahra Wagenknecht zur Ministerpräsidentin Thüringens wählen. Die schlägt das Angebot aus und macht einen Gegenvorschlag.

spiegel.title: Kurilen: Wladimir Putin provoziert Japan mit Besuch auf Inselgruppe
spiegel.description: Im Zweiten Weltkrieg eroberte die Sowjetunion die Kurilen nördlich von Hokkaido, Japan erhebt weiterhin Anspruch auf die Inselgruppe. Nun war Russlands Präsident Putin erstmals dort. Tokio reagierte scharf.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

Guillaume Pley, figure majeure du média Legend à 3,7 millions d’abonnés sur Youtube, est accusé d’avoir envoyé des messages à caractère sexuel à des mineures. Il a porté plainte mercredi pour diffamation envers les médias qui ont relayé ces informations

letemps.description:
La députée new-yorkaise a décidé de rendre public son parcours de PMA à travers plusieurs vidéos publiées sur Instagram. Une décision très scrutée et commentée

letemps.title: Le Tessin suffoque sous une canicule exceptionnelle

phys-org.title: Melting diamond could unlock triple fusion gain and the secrets of ice giant planets
phys-org.description: Diamond is more than a dazzling gem—the extremely hard form of carbon makes up the pellet that encases fuel for inertial confinement fusion, and scientists believe it rains down deep inside ice giant planets like Neptune and Uranus. In both cases, the material experiences enormous pressures. Until now, experiments and simulations have disagreed about how it actually behaves under those conditions.

phys-org.title: Reddit analysis finds AI trust narrowly exceeds distrust, 31% to 26%
phys-org.description: Is generative artificial intelligence technology a helpful tool or a big problem? Nearly four years after ChatGPT became a household name, most people are either using AI applications or generally aware of what the technology can do. But understanding how much they actually trust the work it produces and the answers it provides remains an important question. phys-org.title: Sugar molecule could help protect against dangerous hospital fungus Candida auris
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed a potential new approach against the highly drug-resistant hospital fungus Candida auris. They discovered that a synthetic sugar molecule that is a natural part of the fungus's cell wall, but is not present in humans, could underpin a future vaccine, develop protective antibodies and form the basis of a prototype rapid diagnostic test.

phys-org.title: Fungal age remains elusive as underground networks continually grow, split and recycle
phys-org.description: Some of Earth's oldest living organisms may be right beneath our feet: not ancient trees or coral reefs but fungi. Yet despite their ubiquity and importance, scientists still don't know how long most fungi can live—or even how to define their age.

phys-org.title: Thinking fast and slow: Wild fish reveal how cognition evolved in two closely related species
phys-org.description: Why do two individuals faced with the same information sometimes make completely different decisions? It is a question made famous by Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman, whose book "Thinking, Fast and Slow" explored the contrast between rapid, intuitive decisions and slower, more deliberative thinking in humans.

phys-org.title: Understanding nature's 'dimmer switch': Study sheds new light on how algae regulate photosynthesis with pH
phys-org.description: A new joint study from Constructor University and Princeton University in the Journal of the American Chemical Society focuses on PC645, a protein complex that contributes to cryptophyte algae's ability to photosynthesize efficiently using specialized light-harvesting pigments that can capture energy from dim, blue-green underwater light. During photosynthesis, the pH inside the algae can fluctuate significantly, affecting how they manage light energy.

phys-org.title: A magnetic path to lower-power computing
phys-org.description: From smartphones to data centers, modern electronics rely on billions of tiny switches that consume electricity every time they turn on or off. As global demand for computing continues to grow, so does the energy required to power it. Scientists are therefore searching for alternatives that can perform the same tasks while using far less energy.

phys-org.title: Greater vegetable diversity needed for healthier diets and climate-resilient agriculture
phys-org.description: In a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, researchers show how a wider diversity of vegetables could help improve diets and strengthen agriculture against climate change. They use the term vegetable biodiversity to describe the full range of vegetable species, traditional varieties and their wild relatives.

phys-org.title: Complex suicidal somersault behavior in male redback spiders may be explained by surprisingly simple genetics
phys-org.description: The Australian redback spider (Latrodectus hasselti), a cousin of the North American black widow spider, is known to practice sexual cannibalism, which is somewhat common among spider species. However, the male Australian redback has also been observed facilitating the process with strange moves. Despite the complexity of these behaviors, a new study, published in Biology Letters, indicates that one of these behaviors arises from simple genetics, while another may be more complex.

phys-org.title: Controlling wild pigs can work if it's a group effort
phys-org.description: The federal government is injecting millions of dollars into efforts to combat feral hogs—and it's considering spending even more in the coming years. The problem has grown for decades, but our research has found that a recently revived federal effort offers the potential for bringing the hogs under control.

phys-org.title: Muon g-2 experiment places new constraints on a forbidden property of muons
phys-org.description: A year after its final muon magnetic anomaly announcement, the Muon g-2 collaboration reports a new measurement of a different property of the muon: its electric dipole moment. The work is published on the arXiv preprint server.

phys-org.title: Active supermassive black holes may help form massive planets
phys-org.description: A popular myth about black holes is that they act like giant cosmic vacuum cleaners, sucking in everything around them. But Wladimir Lyra's research found a new mechanism around supermassive black holes that is more like a cosmic nursery, giving birth to planets more massive than Jupiter.

phys-org.title: 'How many will die?': The mysterious ailment killing Kenyan elephants
phys-org.description: Lying on the ground and kicking up a cloud of dust, the elephant slowly exhausted himself in futile attempts to stand, the latest potential victim of a still-mysterious ailment in southern Kenya.

phys-org.title: Mice bred to run three times farther show no fertility or lifespan cost
phys-org.description: Being an elite athlete—at least for a mouse—does not shorten lifespan or limit how many children one can have. This is the finding of a study 30 years in the making, and it runs counter to accepted evolutionary theory.

phys-org.title: Could geothermal roads help prevent potholes before they form? New trial aims to find out
phys-org.description: The U.K.'s pothole problem could one day be tackled from beneath the road surface as researchers at the University of Surrey launch a pioneering trial that uses heat stored underground to keep roads cooler in summer, warmer in winter and less prone to damage.

phys-org.title: Marine heat waves are cooking our ocean ecosystems—and will only become more common
phys-org.description: You may have heard reports of fish die-offs or seen photos of hauntingly bleached coral.

phys-org.title: Early hardship may shape how oxytocin influences altruism
phys-org.description: While humans are inherently social beings, they can interact and connect with others in very different ways. For instance, while some people tend to be more altruistic, others are less prone to helping their friends, acquaintances or even complete strangers, particularly when it comes at a personal cost.

phys-org.title: NZ's new flood maps are missing a hidden threat—the water quietly rising from below
phys-org.description: The latest update of nationwide flood maps, to be released next year, will give communities across New Zealand the clearest picture yet of the regional risk of flooding.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Test
proj-syn.description: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

proj-syn.title: Our AI, Your Problem
proj-syn.description: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

proj-syn.title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
proj-syn.description: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

proj-syn.title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
proj-syn.description: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
proj-syn.description: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

proj-syn.title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
proj-syn.description: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

proj-syn.title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
proj-syn.description: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.
